title: Sales agent: follow Dataverse business skills for your sales processes
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview prerequisites, control paths and API operations are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Work IQ default documentation, cite the source for client opt-in, and identify the sharing checklist step that has no control row.

claims.claim: Business skills are natural-language instructions representing organisational processes, policies and business knowledge.
claims.quote: Business Skills enable organizations to create natural language instructions for Sales Agent to follow, which represent their business processes, policies, and business knowledge.

claims.claim: Business skills are authored and stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: Business Skills are natural language instructions authored and stored in Microsoft Dataverse

claims.claim: The roadmap gives lead qualification, pipeline reviews, account planning, opportunity scoring and account brief creation as example workflows.
claims.quote: Business skills can represent common sales workflows such as lead qualification, pipeline reviews, account planning, opportunity scoring, account brief creation, or organization-specific sales methodologies.

claims.claim: Sellers can interact with Sales agent in natural language.
claims.quote: Sellers can interact with Sales agent using natural language and receive responses that are guided by their organization's Business Skills

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Business skills guide Sales agent's responses according to the organisation's processes and guidance.
claims.quote: Sales Agent uses the instructions in Business Skills to deliver responses that align with the customer's business processes and guidance.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents this as a preview with prerelease documentation subject to change.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: Sales agent discovers and uses business skills with Dynamics 365 data through the Dataverse MCP server after required features are enabled.
claims.quote: After you enable the required Dataverse features, Sales agent can discover and use these skills with your Dynamics 365 data through the Dataverse Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

claims.claim: Enabling Work IQ in the environment enables business skills for agents.
claims.quote: In the Work IQ section, select Turn on Business Applications in Work IQ. This action enables business skills for the environment and allows agents to use them.

claims.claim: Enterprise Copilot Platform is the MCP client Sales agent uses, and its Is Enabled setting must be Yes.
claims.quote: In the Active Allowed MCP Clients list, find Enterprise Copilot Platform and verify that Is Enabled is set to Yes. Its unique name is enterprisecopilotplatform. Sales agent uses this client to access the Dataverse MCP server.

claims.claim: Skill authors can create a business skill in Power Apps.
claims.quote: You can create a business skill in Power Apps in two ways:

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Activating a skill makes its instructions and resources available to agents.
claims.quote: Save and activate | Makes your changes the active version, including its associated resources. The previous active version remains in version history.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents asking Sales agent 'What business skills do I have?' to verify the created skill appears.
claims.quote:
Ask Sales agent, What business skills do I have?

Sales agent should list the skill that you created.

claims.claim: Business skills are not supported when Sales agent is used on mobile.
claims.quote: Business skills aren't supported when you use Sales agent on a mobile device.

claims.claim: A skill must exist, be active and be accessible to the user or agent identity for an agent to discover and use it.
claims.quote:
The skill is active.
The user or agent identity has access to the skill and the required Dataverse data.

claims.claim: Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, with exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:
claims.fix: After this sentence add: 'The general Manage feature settings page still lists Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences as Off by default; check the actual environment setting.' Both sources are already cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/settings-features and https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/business-applications-work-iq/default-settings.

claims.claim: Skills can have attached reference files such as policy documents, standard operating procedures, templates, forms and calculations.
claims.quote: In Resources, select Add Files to attach reference materials that agents need when following the skill, such as policy documents, standard operating procedures, templates, forms, or calculations (20 MB limit).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: General access makes a skill available to everyone in the environment.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Business skills follow Dataverse security patterns.
claims.quote: Business skills are stored in Dataverse and follow Dataverse security patterns.

claims.claim: The same skill permissions apply in Copilot, Work IQ-connected agents and agents connected directly to Dataverse MCP.
claims.quote: The same permissions apply whether you use a skill in Copilot, a Work IQ-connected agent, or an agent connected directly to the Dataverse MCP server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each user who needs business skills needs at least the Basic User security role to see organisation-level skills.
claims.quote: Each user who needs to use business skills has at least the Basic User security role in the Dynamics 365 environment in Power Platform. Without this role, users can't see the organization-level business skills.

claims.claim: Access through a security role requires both that role and the Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.claim: Business skills are not executable code.
claims.quote: Business skills are not executable code. They contain natural-language instructions that guide agent behavior

claims.claim: Agents use their connected tools to carry out a skill's process.
claims.quote: The agent uses its connected tools to carry out the process.

claims.claim: Agent selection of skills is probabilistic, so repeated requests may select differently.
claims.quote: Agent selection is probabilistic, so test representative requests before you share a skill broadly.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Business skills page currently shows no per-skill runtime usage or feedback.
claims.quote: The Business skills page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback.

claims.claim: Changes to the documented Work IQ and MCP access settings apply to new agent interactions.
claims.quote: Changes apply to new agent interactions.

claims.claim: Users might need to refresh an existing session after access-setting changes.
claims.quote: Users might need to refresh an existing session.

claims.quote: Environment Maker | Can create and share skills that they own.

claims.claim: Sales agent must connect to the same Dynamics 365 organisation where business skills were enabled.
claims.quote: Verify that Sales agent is connected to the same Dynamics 365 organization in which you enabled business skills.

claims.claim: The connected Dynamics 365 organisation can be checked under Sources in Sales agent.
claims.quote:
Open Sales agent.
Select Sources.
Verify that Sales agent is connected to the same Dynamics 365 organization in which you enabled business skills.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has a separate preview page for business skills when Sales agent connects to Salesforce.
claims.quote: Enable business skills for Salesforce in the Sales agent (preview)

claims.claim: An environment administrator can manage the environment's Work IQ setting.
claims.quote: Use the environment-level setting to manage business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. You need an environment administrator account.

claims.claim: The Work IQ control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Select Manage, and select the environment.
Select Settings > Product > Features.
Locate Work IQ.
Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no automation that sets the environment Features-page Work IQ toggle at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment feature setting API PowerShell; Dataverse intelligence API enable organization; Power Platform API Work IQ settings update pac admin. Read participation, Features, pac env, API environment settings update; searched organization EntityType for intelligence/Work IQ/skills.

claims.claim: Turning off Work IQ prevents agents using Dataverse business skills in that environment.
claims.quote: On the environment's Features page, turn off the WorkIQ setting. This change prevents agents from using Dataverse business skills in the environment.

claims.claim: The Enterprise Copilot Platform control is reached through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Go to Advanced Settings > Active Allowed MCP Clients > Enterprise Copilot Platform > Is Enabled.
claims.quote:
In the Dataverse Model Context Protocol section, select Go to Advanced Settings.
In the Active Allowed MCP Clients list, find Enterprise Copilot Platform and verify that Is Enabled is set to Yes.

claims.claim: Disabling Enterprise Copilot Platform blocks Sales agent's MCP access.
claims.quote: Block MCP access for Sales agent | In Advanced Settings > Allowed MCP Clients, open Enterprise Copilot Platform, set Is Enabled to No

claims.claim: The all-client MCP control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server (GA version).
claims.quote: In the Dataverse Model Context Protocol section, select Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server (GA version).

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no automation for the environment Features-page all-client MCP toggle at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse MCP server Allow MCP clients GA version enable disable Web API PowerShell; organization MCP IsEnabled; Power Apps administration PowerShell MCP toggle. Read MCP configuration, Features, pac env and API settings update; searched organization EntityType for MCP.

claims.claim: Clearing the environment MCP setting blocks all MCP clients rather than only Sales agent.
claims.quote: Block all MCP clients | On the environment's Features page, clear Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server (GA version).

claims.claim: A skill can be deactivated in Power Apps (maker) through environment > More > Business skills > skill > Deactivate.
claims.quote:
Go to Power Apps and select your environment.
In the left navigation pane, select More, and then select Business skills.
Select a skill, and then select Deactivate from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: PATCH [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/skills(skillid) changes a business skill's active state through statecode.
claims.quote:

Primary key: skillid
Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

0 | Active

claims.claim: Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history while stopping agents discovering or using it.
claims.quote:
To stop agents from discovering or using an active skill:
Select a skill, and then select Deactivate
Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history.
